items.title: Market Minute: Why consumers will pay more for food next year
items.excerpt: Market Minute: Why consumers will pay more for food next year # Market Minute: Why consumers will pay more for food next year Nov. 18, 2026 by Joseph Brusuelas A central narrative for inflation next year will focus on volatile food costs as large manufacturers, challenged by higher input costs, reset prices. Food inflation can take longer to show up in the grocery aisle—longer than it takes, say, for gas prices to show up at the pump. In some cases, it can take more than a year for higher wholesale costs to work their way through North American supply chain networks and become apparent to consumers. But as the calendar moves deeper into next year, some of these higher input costs will have been in effect for many months, suggesting that food-at-home inflation will be an issue for much of next year. In other cases, these higher input costs are passed through more quickly, so consumers will feel the higher prices just in time for the holiday season. Either way, consumer expectations will become a factor. Inflation has exceeded the Federal Reserve’s 2% target for nearly six years, with no relief in sight. If consumers begin to price in this most recent escalation into their own expectations and wage demands, inflation will be pressured higher. In October, food prices in the Consumer Price Index increased by 0.5% on the month. In the same month, the Producer Price Index for food soared by 1.3% with finished consumer foods increasing by 1.6%. In addition, food prices in the PPI have increased by 26% over the past five years. Consumer prices, wholesale inflation and the personal consumption expenditures index, the Federal Reserve’s preferred measure of inflation, have all experienced a sustained increase since late last year on the back of robust consumer demand, trade taxes and the energy shock. A historic disruption in the supply of diesel, fertilizers and other agricultural products derived from distillates has put upward pressure on input costs that in some cases is only now starting to show up in higher inflation. Freight surcharges and reductions in supply because of the cost of agricultural production will all play a role in the food price environment. Transportation service costs have risen by more than 20% this year. The 26.7% increase in fresh and dry vegetables on a seasonally adjusted basis in October was one of the eye-popping increases in inflation linked to the latest phase of the energy shock that began in March. But those price increases will not be passed through to consumers on a one-to-one basis. Rather, they will be partially absorbed through thinner retailer margins as stores try to retain loyal customers and as large retailers resist significant price increases from vendors. Although diesel is up more than 59.2% since the start of Middle East hostilities, it is down roughly 8.3% since the $6.52 peak on Sept. 21, and that may partially mitigate the sharp increases over the past few months. Diesel prices tend to peak in the fall and ease in the winter. ## Near term price increases *Fresh produce and perishables: 1 to 4 weeks* Fresh produce like tomatoes, lettuce and fresh greens, which are transported on large, refrigerated trucks fueled by diesel, have observed large price increases that are either absorbed through retailer margins or passed through to consumers. ... *Dry and packaged goods 4 to 12 weeks* Costs associated with canned produce and dry goods such as potatoes, onions and dried beans that can be stored in large facilities often operate under negotiated contracts. As such they are more insensitive to month-to-month price increases. ... As inventories of dry and packaged goods are purchased or reach expiration dates, then those new contracts at ... ## The takeaway Food prices are likely to rise into the holiday season and well into next year. While food prices are volatile from month to month, they are up approximately 26% since 2021, and it is likely that the government will be looking for ways to reduce those costs. But before the government can do much of anything, it is highly likely that large food manufacturers will increase prices during the first three months of the year as inventory costs reset higher. While we expect overall inflation in the Consumer Price Index to ease back to 2.9% next year because of friendly year-ago base effects, the public may not buy that as they experience rising prices early in the year.

items.title: Fed’s Waller says central bank may need to ‘shock people’ with half-point rate hike
items.excerpt: # Fed’s Waller says central bank may need to ‘shock people’ with half-point rate hike Published Wed, Nov 18 2026 7:20 AM ESTUpdated 5 Min Ago ... Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller on Wednesday called for aggressive action against inflation, which he said has been more persistent than he expected. In the near term, the policymaker told CNBC in a live interview that a half-percentage-point increase in the Fed's benchmark rate is probably necessary at the Dec. 8-9 meeting of the Federal Open Market Committee. From here, he said the Fed needs to reverse the three quarter-point reductions from last year and may need to do more. "You might need to, like, shock people," Waller told CNBC's Steve Liesman during the "Squawk Box" interview. "I'm very, very concerned about inflation. It's kind of headed in the wrong direction, and it's spreading out," he said. "If you really want to get it down, you've got to start taking more aggressive actions." Futures prices are fully pricing in a quarter percentage point hike at the Federal Open Market Committee's Dec. 8-9 meeting. They also are anticipating another move in January, followed by at least one additional increase before the end of 2027, according to the CME Group's FedWatch gauge.

Raye earned 11 Grammy nominations including nods for song and record of the year for "Husband," and for album of the ‌year for "This Music May Contain Hope." Rosalia racked up nine nominations, days after she dominated the Latin Grammys with her album "Lux." ... items.title: Entertainment News Today, 18 Nov 2026: Detty December | Nigeria's Fast-Growing Online Forum For News & Discussions
items.excerpt: Good morning. December in Lagos is filling up fast, with Lauryn Hill now confirmed for Detty December and Nigeria’s own stars booking venues across the city. Olamide’s new album has gone straight to the top of the chart, investors have told Nollywood what it takes to get their money, and Chioma Chukwuka has been honoured in Houston. ## Today at a glance - Lauryn Hill to headline Detty December Fest in Lagos on 21 December; Wizkid opens the festival on 18 December. - Olamide’s Time and Space goes to number one on Apple Music Nigeria. - Film companies at the AFRIFF market seek between $250,000 and $5 million from investors. - Chioma Chukwuka receives a Lifetime Achievement Award in Texas. - Actress Linda Osifo announces her engagement. - Joeboy’s Lavida Boy EP arrives on 20 November. ... American singer Lauryn Hill will headline Detty December Fest at Detty Village in Ilubirin, Ikoyi, on Monday 21 December, joined by her sons YG Marley and Zion Marley. The 13-day festival, produced by Livespot360, runs from 18 to 30 December, with Wizkid billed for the opening night and Summer Walker and Fridayy on 27 December. Separately, Flytime Promotions has Brandy on 20 December and Lil Baby, Kehlani and Yung Miami on 21 December at Eko Convention Centre. Nigerian acts have their own dates: Davido’s three-night residency at the National Theatre runs 17 to 19 December, Asake plays Lagos on 20 December and Adekunle Gold stages his show on 26 December. ... Olamide’s 13th studio album, Time and Space, reached number one on the Apple Music Nigeria Top Albums chart within about a day of release. The 10-track project, released through YBNL Nation and EMPIRE, has one guest, FOLA, and Olamide says he painted the cover art himself. Asake, a former YBNL signee, reshared the cover on his Instagram story, even though he is not on the line-up for Olamide’s YBNL reunion concert in December. That show features Adekunle Gold, Fireboy DML, Lil Kesh, Young Jonn, Pheelz and DJ Enimoney. ... Ten African film, animation and streaming companies pitched to investors at the ... Joeboy’s new single Pretty Girls peaked at number 61 on Spotify Nigeria’s daily songs chart with about 61,000 streams, and it has become the most Shazamed song in Kenya. The track leads into his five-track Lavida Boy EP, due on Friday 20 November.
